paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God stays the same, and that's the only reason anybody is still standing. The LORD says, "Because I, the LORD, do not change, you descendants of Jacob have not been destroyed" (Malachi 3:6). The people had been drifting for generations, and He still held on. That means your story with Him doesn't rest on how steady YOU are.

So when He says, "Return to Me, and I will return to you," the door is wide open (Malachi 3:7). Their question, "How can we return?", gets a very practical answer: tithes and offerings (Malachi 3:7-8). I think that's God showing that turning back isn't just a warm feeling, it shows up in what we do with what we hold. And I'll be honest, I hold my cookie dough pretty tight sometimes, so I'm talking to myself too.

Then comes the invitation that still gets me: "Test Me in this," says the LORD of Hosts (Malachi 3:10). He promises to "pour out for you blessing without measure" and to rebuke the devourer so the fruit of their land is kept safe (Malachi 3:10-11). So bring the full amount, trust Him with the rest, and watch what He does. Giving isn't paying God off, friend, it's trusting the One who never changes.
